basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 11.' and it opens 'Vers. 11. Modicum resinae. Resinam gummi dicimus, quo nomine generaliter omnes arbores'. The printing states no chapter here and the lemma is too short to match, so the chapter is the one the preceding block established.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 11. Modicum resinae. Resinam gummi dicimus, quo nomine generaliter omnes arbores vocantur; sed hic intelligitur species quae sic proprio nomine dicitur Stiracis. Stiracis genus est resinae. Pro stirace LXX thymiama posuerunt, quod Hebraice dicitur NECHOTA. Stacte gutta myrrhae arboris. Terebinthus arbor, cujus resina similiter vocatur
